concept_name: Congruent: one lands exactly on the other

item.question: Figures that are exact copies of each other, with the same shape and size, are said to be congruent. Congruent figures can be placed one exactly over the other. Test the two curvy shapes and the two round discs with a wedge cut out.
steps: Trace the first curvy shape on tracing paper and carry the tracing over to the second shape.
Drop it on the second shape: every edge coincides and there is no gap, so the two curvy shapes are congruent.
Do the same with the two round discs: the tracing lands exactly, so that pair is congruent too.
Size means every length and every angle, so the test is landing exactly, not looking alike.
item.answer: Both pairs are congruent: in each pair the tracing of one figure lands exactly on the other.

item.question: What would you measure to copy a circle, and what would you measure to copy a rectangle? How would you check that two of each are congruent?
steps_tex: A circle is fixed by one measurement, the radius. The diameter does the same job, because it is twice the radius.
Two circles are congruent exactly when their radii are equal. That one comparison is the whole check.
A rectangle is fixed by two measurements, the length and the breadth. Every corner is already a right angle.
Two rectangles are congruent exactly when both the lengths match and the breadths match. A rectangle of six by four and one of four by six are congruent, because one is the other turned.

concept_name: The two circles, and why both answers are the same

item.question: Is it enough to know the three sides, four centimetres, six centimetres and eight centimetres? Can you draw such a triangle?
steps: Draw the base AB of 6 cm.
The corner must be 4 cm from A, so it lies on a circle of radius 4 cm around A.
The corner must be 8 cm from B, so it lies on a circle of radius 8 cm around B.
The circles cross in two places, E above the line AB and F below it. Each crossing is 4 cm from A and 8 cm from B.
Join E to A and to B. The triangle ABE has sides 6 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm, so such a triangle can be drawn.
item.answer: Yes. A triangle with sides 4 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm can be drawn. The two circles cross at the corner, and the angles come out as about 104.5 degrees at A, 29 degrees at B and 46.6 degrees at E.

concept_name: The two circles, and why both answers are the same

item.question: The two circles cross at E and F. Examine whether triangle ABE and triangle ABF are congruent. You may trace and compare, cut out and place one on the other, or notice that AB is a fold line.
steps: Both triangles have the base AB = 6 cm, and AE = AF = 4 cm and BE = BF = 8 cm, because E and F are both crossing points of the same two circles.
E and F are mirror images across the line AB: they sit the same distance above and below it.
Fold the paper along AB and E lands exactly on F, so triangle ABE lands exactly on triangle ABF.
A flip is allowed, so the two triangles are congruent, with A on A, B on B and E on F.
So all triangles with the same three side lengths are congruent: this is the SSS condition.
item.answer: Yes, triangle ABE is congruent to triangle ABF, because one is the other flipped over the line AB. If two triangles have the same three sides, they are congruent (SSS).

item.question: If two triangles have the same side lengths, then they are congruent. This is called the SSS condition for congruence. Do the sides five, eight, eleven and eleven, five, eight make twins? Do six, six, nine and six, nine, nine?
steps: Match five with five, eight with eight and eleven with eleven. All three sides have a partner, so the first pair are twins.
In six, six, nine and six, nine, nine, one six pairs with one six and the nine pairs with one nine.
The second six has no partner and the second nine has no partner, so only two of the three sides match.
The SSS condition needs all three sides to match, so the second pair are not twins.
item.answer: Five, eight, eleven and eleven, five, eight are twins. Six, six, nine and six, nine, nine are not twins.
